text.p: These are some of the leading stories in Israeli newspapers on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Plea bargain with legislator Aryeh Deri collapsed because prosecution insisted bribery charge be included.
- Palestinian suspected of selling land to Israelis murdered in Ramallah.
- U.S. ambassador to Israel: Israel-PLO Oslo accord has broken down.
- Water Commission: Don't break up Mekorot monopoly.
- Cellcom's first quarter net profit up sharply to 86.9 million shekels.
- Israeli army: We will target the Lebanese army if it fires again on our forces.
- Pressure on Netanyahu to sack justice minister and appoint Yaakov Neeman.
- U.S. may freeze its involvement in Middle East peace talks.
- Sharp rise of 2.3 percent in money supply in April.
- Senior officials at K.A.L.-Visa questioned over contracts with businesses.
